classification.difficultyReason: Rearrange inequalities with two nonzero sides, factor the resulting quadratics, sketch their opening directions and zeroes, and select inside or outside intervals with correct endpoint inclusion.

content.prompt: Draw appropriate graphs to solve the following quadratic inequalities.

answer.worked:
Sketch $y=(2-x)(x+4)$. Its intercepts are $x=-4$ and $x=2$, and the parabola opens downwards. The graph lies below the $x$-axis outside the intercepts.
$$x<-4\quad\text{or}\quad x>2.$$

spec.description: Solution sketch of the downward-opening quadratic, with its two zeroes marked. No grid.

answer.worked:
$$x^2-3x+2=(x-1)(x-2).$$
Sketch $y=x^2-3x+2$. The upward-opening parabola meets the $x$-axis at $1$ and $2$. It is on or above the axis outside these intercepts.
$$x\leq1\quad\text{or}\quad x\geq2.$$

spec.description: Upward-opening quadratic with both zeroes marked.

answer.worked:
$$x^2+2x=x(x+2).$$
Sketch $y=x^2+2x$. The upward-opening parabola has zeroes $-2$ and $0$. It lies below the $x$-axis between them. Both endpoints are excluded.
$$-2<x<0.$$

spec.description: Upward-opening quadratic used after moving both sides to the left.

answer.worked:
$$x^2-x-6=(x+2)(x-3).$$
Sketch $y=x^2-x-6$. The upward-opening parabola has zeroes $-2$ and $3$. It lies on or below the $x$-axis between these intercepts.
$$-2\leq x\leq3.$$

$$12x-x^2=x(12-x).$$
Sketch $y=12x-x^2$. The downward-opening parabola has zeroes $0$ and $12$. It lies on or above the $x$-axis between these intercepts.
$$0\leq x\leq12.$$

$$\begin{align*}x^2-4&\geq-2x+4\\x^2+2x-8&\geq0.\end{align*}$$
Sketch $y=x^2+2x-8=(x+4)(x-2)$. The parabola opens upwards and is on or above the $x$-axis outside its zeroes $-4$ and $2$.
$$x\leq-4\quad\text{or}\quad x\geq2.$$

spec.description: Upward-opening quadratic obtained by subtracting the right-hand side.
